Roxbury, NY
~3 hours from NYC
Make a weekend of it

Travel & Stay

Roxbury is in the western Catskills, about three hours from NYC, two from Albany, and four from Philadelphia. We highly recommend coming up Friday and staying through Sunday — the area is gorgeous and worth more than 24 hours.

Where to sleep

Three places we like, at different price points

We’ve held a small room block at the Lazy Crow Inn and the Catskill Lodge under “Hesse-Tran / Okafor.” Both will run shuttles to the venue. Book by August 1 for the held rate.

Lazy Crow Inn

$$$

8 minutes to venue · Block held under “Hesse-Tran”

A 12-room boutique inn in a restored 1890s Victorian on the edge of town. Bathtubs you’d actually want to take a bath in, a generous breakfast that includes an excellent egg sandwich, and a small bar where most of our families will probably end up after the wedding. About $325/night for the held block.

lazycrowinn.example →

Catskill Lodge

$$

12 minutes to venue · Block held under “Okafor”

A converted ski lodge that leans Scandi-cozy: shared sauna, a small lap pool, and a fireplace that is somehow always going. Rooms are smaller and lighter on amenities than the Lazy Crow but the vibe is great and the breakfast (a long buffet with very good yogurt) is included. About $215/night.

catskilllodge.example →

AirBnB & cabin rentals

$

10–25 minutes to venue · Best with 2+ people splitting

There are a ton of well-priced cabins, A-frames, and farmhouses on AirBnB and VRBO within a 20-minute drive of Roxbury — especially in Halcottsville, Margaretville, and Andes. If you’re a group of 4+, this is often the best deal. Search “Roxbury, NY” with check-in Friday September 18 and check-out Sunday September 20.

Heads up: if you go this route, plan to drive yourself or carpool — we can’t run shuttles to private rentals.

Getting here

How to get to Roxbury

  • A

    Drive from NYC

    About 3 hours via I-87 N to NY-28 W. Easy drive, mostly scenic once you’re past Kingston. Gas up in Kingston — it gets sparse after that. Parking at the venue is plentiful and free.

  • B

    Trailways bus to Margaretville

    The Adirondack Trailways line runs from Port Authority to Margaretville (about 4 hours, $58 one way). From Margaretville it’s a 15-minute Uber to either hotel — or text us in advance and we’ll arrange a pickup with one of the welcome-bag crew.

  • C

    Amtrak to Hudson, then drive

    Amtrak’s Empire Service from NY Penn to Hudson, NY takes about 2 hours and is a beautiful ride along the river. Hudson to Roxbury is then ~1h 20m by car. Hertz and Enterprise both have offices a 10-minute walk from the Hudson station.

  • D

    Flying in

    Closest major airports are Albany (ALB, ~1h 50m drive) and Stewart (SWF, ~2h 10m). Both have rental cars on-site. For coast-to-coast travelers, JFK or LGA + a rental car is your best bet — flights into Albany from the west coast are often surprisingly expensive.

  • E

    Carpool from NYC

    We’re going to set up a shared spreadsheet in mid-August for anyone who wants to coordinate rides up from the city. If you’d like to be on it, mention it in your RSVP. Splitting a car 4 ways is dramatically cheaper than the bus and faster than the train.

If you’re making a weekend

What to do nearby

We’ve spent a lot of weekends up here over the last two years. Here’s the short list of what we’d send you to.

Hike

Pratt Rock Trail

A 1.2-mile out-and-back in Prattsville with a wildly weird hand-carved cliffside monument at the top. Best underrated short hike in the area. 25 minutes from the venue.

Easy · 1 hour
Hike

Plattekill Mountain Loop

A proper Catskills hike — 5 miles, 1,800 ft of gain, summit views in every direction. Pack water and snacks; there is nothing at the top but a great view. 35 minutes from the venue.

Moderate · 3–4 hours
Swim

Big Pond & Little Pond

A pair of crystal-clear glacial ponds in the state forest about 20 minutes south of Roxbury. Free, sandy beach, extremely few crowds in September.

Bring a towel · Free
Eat

Phoenicia Diner

The reference standard for Catskills breakfast. Get the brisket hash. About 40 minutes from Roxbury but worth it if you’re passing through on the way back.

All day · $$
Eat

Peekamoose Restaurant & Tap Room

Big-night-out tasting menu in a converted farmhouse. Reservations a must, especially on a Friday. This is also where we’re doing our Friday welcome dinner.

Dinner · $$$
Coffee

Roxbury Coffee Co.

The town’s only real coffee shop, in a converted church annex on Main Street. Excellent flat white, very good almond croissant, slightly slow service that we’ve grown to love.

7am–2pm · $
Drink

West Kill Brewing

Farm brewery in a 1700s barn 35 minutes east. Mostly hazy IPAs and saisons, all good. Tasting room is dog-friendly and there’s a small food menu (the smashburger is a great choice).

Thu–Sun · $$
Drink

Union Grove Distillery

Small-batch spirits in Arkville, 12 minutes west. Free tastings, friendly owners, and a maple bourbon that made it into our welcome bags.

Wed–Sun · $
See

Roxbury Arts Group

A really lovely little arts nonprofit in the center of town that runs a year-round gallery, a small theater, and a packed event calendar. Worth a 30-minute stop if there’s a show up.

Open Fri–Sun · Free
See

Kaaterskill Falls

A two-tier waterfall about 50 minutes from Roxbury — one of the most photographed spots in the Catskills. Wear shoes with grip; the rocks at the lookout get slick.

Free · 1–2 hours

More ideas? Text us. We have opinions about every general store in a 30-mile radius.
